name: Sohar
title: Sohar Ship UTM: Hull Thickness Gauging for Bulk Carriers
description: Hull thickness gauging at Sohar Port, Oman: UTM on ore carrier and bulk carrier holds, ESP renewal survey preparation, tanker and scrubber piping checks.
h1: Hull Thickness Gauging and Ship Inspection at Sohar Port and Freezone
intro: Sohar Port and Freezone is Oman's industrial port on the Gulf of Oman, built around iron ore, aluminium, steel, refining and petrochemical plants that move bulk and liquid cargo in and out. Very large ore carriers discharging at the iron ore terminal, tankers at the liquid berths and container ships at the box terminal all pass through. We mobilise a team from India to Sohar to gauge holds, tanks, hull structure and piping, timed around a discharge, a wait at anchorage or a docking further down the coast.
keywords: hull thickness gauging at sohar port

highlights.h: Ore carrier holds under heavy duty
highlights.p: Iron ore is dense and discharged by grab, so tank tops, hopper plates and lower frames on large ore carriers take both mechanical damage and corrosion. We gauge those areas during discharge and add crack detection at hopper knuckles and frame brackets.

Sohar lies on the Gulf of Oman, not far from the Fujairah anchorage, so ships can be gauged here without entering the Gulf. That suits owners planning work between Gulf calls and a docking in the UAE or at Duqm.

One visit to Sohar can involve very different ships: an ore carrier, a product tanker loading refinery output, a container ship at the box terminal. We size the team and the equipment to the vessel and its berth window.

port.h: Sohar Port and Freezone: Industry and Shipping
p: Sohar Port is a joint venture between the Government of Oman and the Port of Rotterdam, with a freezone alongside, and it was developed to host heavy industry rather than to serve a city. Its tenants include Vale's iron ore pelletising plant and distribution centre, an aluminium smelter, steel plants, the OQ refinery and petrochemical units, and their trade dominates the port: iron ore in and pellets out, alumina and aluminium, steel products, crude feedstock, refined products and chemicals. Hutchison Ports Sohar runs the container terminal, and general cargo, dry bulk and liquid bulk terminals handle the rest.

The ships that matter most for gauging are the very large ore carriers bringing Brazilian ore to the Vale terminal. Discharging a ship of that size takes days alongside, holds open up one after another as the grabs reach the tank top, and an incoming ship may lie at anchorage before berthing. Tankers loading refinery and petrochemical cargoes at the liquid berths have shorter stays but often wait offshore for a slot. Container ships at the box terminal keep to their service schedules, so their work is selective. Because the port sits outside the Strait of Hormuz, some owners use a Sohar call to complete gauging they did not want to schedule inside the Gulf.

Ore carriers concentrate the inspection problem. Iron ore loads the double bottom and hopper structure heavily, grabs and front loaders gouge the tank top and lower frames, and hold coatings rarely survive long. Add the warm, humid conditions of the Batinah coast and ballast tanks filled with warm Gulf of Oman water, and wastage builds in exactly the areas that the bulk carrier enhanced survey rules, IACS UR Z10.2 or Z10.5 depending on the hull arrangement, target at renewal. Fatigue cracking at hopper knuckles and frame end brackets is a separate risk that thickness readings alone will not show, which is why magnetic particle testing belongs in the same visit.

facilities.h: Where Gauging Takes Place at Sohar
p: Sohar has no drydock of its own, so work here is done afloat. The iron ore terminal gives the longest access, as holds empty during a discharge that runs over several days; we work behind the discharge, gauging each hold once the grabs have cleared the tank top and the stevedores allow access. On tankers at the liquid berths, the terminal's rules limit what can happen alongside, and cargo-area work is usually better done at the anchorage. General cargo and dry bulk berths offer stays long enough for hold and deck gauging on smaller bulk carriers and multipurpose ships, and container ships at Hutchison Ports Sohar can take selective gauging inside the cargo window.

When a Sohar ship needs a drydock, the usual options are Asyad Drydock at Duqm, further down the Omani coast, or the UAE yards to the north. Gauging the holds and ballast tanks during the Sohar discharge, while the ship is empty and the holds are open, gives the repair yard a measured steel list before the ship sails for docking. That matters most for large ore carriers, where steel renewal in the hold area can be extensive and the yard needs time to prepare plate and labour.
list: Iron ore terminal — hold, tank top, hopper plate and frame gauging on very large ore carriers as each hold is cleared during discharge
Liquid bulk berths — deck, piping and accessible tank gauging on product and chemical tankers, within the terminal's safety rules
Hutchison Ports Sohar container terminal — selective deck, hatch coaming and scrubber piping gauging on container ships during the cargo window
General cargo and dry bulk berths — hold and deck gauging on bulk carriers and multipurpose ships carrying steel, aluminium and other industrial cargo
Sohar anchorage — condition, pre-purchase and on-hire gauging on ships waiting for a berth, reached by launch
Asyad Drydock, Duqm — pre-docking gauging done at Sohar for ships continuing down the coast to dock; see our Duqm page

context.h: Port State Control, Sulphur and Owner Context at Sohar
p: Oman is a member of the Riyadh MoU, and port state control inspections at Sohar follow that regime. The Gulf of Oman is not an emission control area, so the global 0.50% sulphur limit applies, and many of the large ore carriers and tankers calling at Sohar run exhaust gas scrubbers. Scrubber overboard lines and wash-water piping on these ships carry acidic water at high temperature and are a regular gauging item, especially where the overboard penetration passes through ballast or void spaces. Rules on discharging open-loop wash water vary between ports and change over time, so confirm the current position for Sohar with the ship's agent.

Much of the ore carrier fleet serving the Vale distribution centre is owned and managed in East Asia and works under long-term contracts, and both the owners and the charterer watch hold structure closely. Owners of bulk carriers approaching the third renewal survey, with its extensive gauging of holds and ballast tanks, gain from having condition data well before the survey date. For tankers, oil-major vetting and CAP requests apply here as anywhere else. For owners looking for thickness measurement in Oman, Sohar's position also makes it easy to coordinate with work at the Fujairah anchorage just up the coast or with a later docking at Duqm.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at Sohar
jobs.p: Ultrasonic thickness gauging in Sohar follows the cargo. The long ore discharges give the best access the port offers for hold structure, while tanker and container work is fitted into shorter windows or moved to the anchorage. Most jobs prepare an owner for a renewal survey or a docking, or give a buyer or charterer measured condition data. A single mobilisation can often cover more than one ship in port, if their windows line up.
list: A very large ore carrier discharging at the Vale terminal: tank top, hopper plate and lower frame gauging hold by hold, with magnetic particle testing at hopper knuckles, ahead of its third renewal survey
A bulk carrier loading pellets for regional steelmakers: hold frame and side shell gauging to estimate steel renewal before it sails for docking
A product tanker at the Sohar anchorage before loading refinery cargo: CAP-scope gauging of cargo tank deckheads, bottom plating and ballast tanks for a charterer
A container ship on its scheduled call: scrubber wash-water and overboard piping gauged within the cargo window, with readings compared against the owner's previous records
A bulk carrier changing hands at anchorage: pre-purchase gauging of holds, hatch covers and ballast tanks for the buyer's superintendent

logistics: Teams fly into Muscat International Airport, which has direct services from many Indian cities, and drive north along the Batinah coast to Sohar. Sohar Port and the freezone are security-controlled, so the ship's agent arranges passes for the technicians and their equipment, and launch transfers for anchorage work. Indian technicians need an Omani visa for business travel, which we apply for once the ship's arrival is confirmed. Ore discharges are usually scheduled well ahead, which helps when booking flights and passes for an India-based team.

faqs.q: Can you gauge the holds of a large ore carrier while it discharges at Sohar?
faqs.a: Yes. We work behind the discharge, gauging each hold once the grabs have cleared the tank top and the stevedores release it. Holds that are still working, or that open only at the end of discharge, are done last. The scope usually covers tank top, hopper plating, lower frames and brackets, with magnetic particle testing at known crack-prone connections. Agree the sequence with the terminal and the master before arrival.

faqs.q: Why gauge at Sohar rather than inside the Gulf?
faqs.a: Sohar is on the Gulf of Oman, so a ship can be gauged without transiting the Strait of Hormuz. For owners trading between the Gulf and the Indian Ocean, or planning a docking at Duqm or in the UAE, a Sohar call can be the point in the voyage where the ship is empty, accessible and close to its next yard.

faqs.q: What should we gauge on scrubber piping for ships calling at Sohar?
faqs.a: Concentrate on the wash-water discharge line from the scrubber to the overboard, the overboard penetration and distance piece, and the valve bodies on that line, particularly where they pass through ballast tanks or voids. Warm, acidic wash water thins steel quickly and a leak there can flood a space. We take grid readings around bends and welds, where thinning usually starts.

faqs.q: Can one mobilisation cover several ships at Sohar?
faqs.a: Often, yes. If two or more of your ships are in Sohar or nearby within the same period, we can sequence the work for one team, provided each ship's agent has the technicians on its pass list. We confirm the plan with each master in advance, since the ore terminal, the liquid berths and the anchorage keep different schedules.
